connect.title: Connect a number
connect.intro: Add as many as you need. Several Twilio numbers and MSG91 senders can run at once.
connect.providerHint: Twilio for most countries; MSG91 for reliable delivery into India.
connect.fromHint: A number in international format (Twilio) or your registered sender (MSG91). A sender made of letters is one-way: no replies.
connect.sidHint: Twilio only. Leave blank to reuse the keys already connected for WhatsApp.
connect.tokenHint: Saved encrypted. For Twilio, leave blank to reuse the keys already connected for WhatsApp.
connect.dltTemplateHint: MSG91 only. The approved DLT template id used for Indian delivery.

connect.rateHint: For your SMS spend reporting only. Never billed to the WhatsApp wallet.

twilio.title: Twilio (global)
twilio.p1: Copy the Account SID (it starts with AC) and the Auth Token from the Twilio console home page. An API key starting with SK will not work.
twilio.p2: Buy an SMS-capable number, or use your trial number, and paste it as the From number in international format.
twilio.p3: In the Twilio number's settings, paste the delivery-report address above as the status callback URL.
twilio.p4: Trial accounts can only text verified numbers and refuse custom text.

msg91.title: MSG91 (India / DLT)
msg91.p1: Indian carriers filter foreign long-code numbers, so use MSG91 for reliable delivery into India.
msg91.p2: Paste your MSG91 Auth Key in the Auth Token field.
msg91.p3: On the DLT portal, register a 6-letter sender id and a message template, then paste both in the DLT options.
msg91.p4: With a DLT template id the sender uses MSG91's template route; without one it sends plain text.

billing.title: Segments, cost and billing
billing.p1: A text of up to 160 plain characters is one segment (GSM-7). One emoji or non-Latin character drops the limit to 70 (UCS-2) and can triple the cost.
billing.p2: Longer texts are split into segments of 153 characters (67 with UCS-2), and each segment is billed.
billing.p3: The rate you enter is for spend reporting only. Texts are metered by your plan's monthly SMS quota, never the WhatsApp wallet.
billing.p4: A sender id made of letters is one-way and is not accepted in every country, for example the US and Canada.

segments.ucs2: This message contains characters outside the GSM alphabet (emoji or non-Latin script), so it is limited to {perSegment} characters per SMS and will be billed as {segments} messages.

compose.note: SMS sends plain text only. A header, footer, attachment, buttons and split testing are not used, so they are hidden.
compose.bodyHint: Keep it short: every 160 characters is another segment, and each segment is billed.

chooser.name: SMS
chooser.hint: Text your contacts from a Twilio number or an MSG91 sender.

operator.title: SMS channel
operator.superOnly: Only a super admin can change the SMS switch. You can see its state.
operator.explanation: Turns the SMS channel on or off for every workspace. It only shows or hides the entry points (the SMS menu, the sender pickers and the SMS template channel). Senders, templates and sends already running are never deleted or stopped.

state.enabled: SMS is on. Workspaces whose plan includes SMS can connect senders and send text messages from broadcasts and campaigns.
state.disabled: SMS is off. Workspaces do not see the SMS menu, sender pickers or SMS templates. Turn it on when you are ready to offer the channel.

operator.enabledToast: SMS is now enabled for the platform.
operator.disabledToast: SMS is now disabled for the platform.

disableDialog.title: Disable SMS?
disableDialog.body: Every workspace stops seeing the SMS menu, sender pickers and SMS templates straight away. Nothing is deleted, and senders that exist keep working. You can turn it back on at any time.
